description: We are Team GeoSonic, a team of five members participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are working on the Earth Information Jukebox challenge to turn Earth data into interesting sounds. We are interested in space, Earth science, coding, creativity, and teamwork. We welcome team members who are interested in coding, data analysis, sound design, research, and presentation.
summary:
TerraEcho – Earth's Living Soundscape

TerraEcho is an interactive web-based project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge The Earth Information Jukebox. Its main goal is to transform real NASA Earth science observations into meaningful visual experiences and sounds.

The project focuses on two major datasets: NASA Black Marble, which represents changing global night-time lights from 2012 to 2023, and NASA OSCAR with GHRSST MUR, which provides information about global ocean surface currents and sea-surface temperatures.

TerraEcho features an interactive 3D-style Earth globe, scientific data visualizations, historical timelines, and an audio sonification system that converts environmental measurements into sound. Users can explore observations, switch between datasets, listen to Earth's data through a sound player, and view real-time waveforms and frequency spectrums.

It also provides a data upload and validation system that supports CSV, TSV, JSON, and GeoJSON formats. Overall, TerraEcho combines science, technology, visualization, and sound to make complex Earth observations more engaging, interactive, and easier to understand.
details:
TerraEcho – Earth's Living Soundscape is an interactive web-based project that transforms NASA Earth observation data into an immersive visual and audio experience. It uses NASA Black Marble satellite data to explore changes in global night-time lights from 2012 to 2023 and NASA OSCAR ocean current data along with sea-surface temperature information to visualize ocean dynamics.

The platform features an interactive 3D-style Earth explorer, global data visualizations, year-based comparisons, ocean current animations, and a sound player that converts scientific observations into ambient soundscapes. Users can explore changes in Earth's environment through both visual and auditory experiences.

TerraEcho is designed to make complex Earth science data more accessible, engaging, and understandable. It was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with interactive visualizations, data processing, and Web Audio API technology.
